Gall dual RNA-seq — results overview¶

Every figure here is built from files the make pipeline wrote; nothing is recomputed from reads. Run top to bottom.

Stage Source files
Trimming 01_trim/*.fastp.json
Alignment 02_align/*.hisat2.log, 02_align/*.idxstats
Dual-fraction split logs/mapping_fractions.tsv
Counting 03_counts/*.txt.summary
Expression 04_matrix/*.tsv
Metadata samples.tsv

Read section 4 before interpreting anything as "bacterial expression."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot theme. Categorical hues are assigned in a fixed order and never cycled:
# a host keeps its colour in every figure, whatever subset is on screen.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SERIES = ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100",
          "#e87ba4", "#008300", "#4a3aa7", "#e34948"]
SURFACE, INK, INK2, GRID = "#fcfcfb", "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e6e5e1"
# single-hue blue ramp, light -> dark, for magnitude (heatmaps)
BLUES = ["#cde2fb", "#b7d3f6", "#9ec5f4", "#86b6ef", "#6da7ec", "#5598e7",
         "#3987e5", "#2a78d6", "#256abf", "#1c5cab", "#184f95", "#104281", "#0d366b"]
SEQ = mpl.colors.LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("seq_blue", BLUES)

mpl.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": SURFACE, "axes.facecolor": SURFACE, "savefig.facecolor": SURFACE,
    "figure.dpi": 110, "savefig.dpi": 150, "savefig.bbox": "tight",
    "font.size": 9, "text.color": INK,
    "axes.edgecolor": GRID, "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.titlesize": 11,
    "axes.titleweight": "semibold", "axes.titlecolor": INK, "axes.titlelocation": "left",
    "axes.titlepad": 10, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID, "grid.linewidth": 0.8,
    "xtick.color": INK2, "ytick.color": INK2, "xtick.labelsize": 8, "ytick.labelsize": 8,
    "legend.frameon": False, "legend.fontsize": 8,
    "lines.linewidth": 2, "lines.markersize": 8,
})

def clean(ax, axis="x"):
    """Recessive frame: grid on the measure axis only, no top/right spines."""
    hide = {"x": ("top", "right", "left"), "y": ("top", "right", "bottom"),
            "both": ("top", "right")}[axis]
    for side in hide:
        ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
    ax.grid(axis=axis, alpha=0.9)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    return ax

def note(ax, text, y=-0.34):
    ax.text(0, y, text, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7.5, color=INK2,
            va="top", ha="left", wrap=True)

def save(fig, name):
    fig.savefig(FIGDIR / f"{name}.png")
    return fig

thousands = FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:,.0f}")

1. Samples¶

14 galls: two Agrobacterium strains (1416, 29), three genotypes (wild type plus two 1416 mutants, G-19 and G-30), across six host plant species and gall ages from 26 to 635 days. Sample naming is <strain><genotype><hostcode><age>.

def host_legend(ax, hosts=None, y=-0.17, ncols=3):
    """Legend below the plot: with 14 sorted bars there is no free space inside."""
    hosts = hosts if hosts is not None else HOST_ORDER
    handles = [mpl.patches.Patch(facecolor=HOST_COLOR[h], label=h) for h in hosts]
    ax.legend(handles=handles, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0, y),
              ncols=ncols, borderaxespad=0, columnspacing=1.4)

def barh(ax, labels, values, colors, fmt="{:,.0f}", pad=0.02, log=False):
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    y = np.arange(len(labels))
    ax.barh(y, values, height=0.62, color=colors)      # height<1 leaves a gap between bars
    ax.set_yticks(y, labels)
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    span = values.max() if len(values) else 1
    for yi, v in zip(y, values):
        # offset has to be multiplicative on a log axis, additive on a linear one
        x = v * 1.12 if log else v + span * pad
        ax.text(x, yi, fmt.format(v), va="center", fontsize=7.5, color=INK2)
    if not log:
        ax.set_xlim(0, span * 1.18)
    return clean(ax, "x")

fastp numbers, per sample. Depth is even (44–86 M pairs) and quality is high across the board — nothing here explains the differences that appear later.

3. Alignment to the combined reference¶

Each sample was aligned to a combined index — its host genome plus the Agrobacterium genome of the strain it carries — so a read competes between plant and bacterium in one pass instead of being assigned twice.

The alignment rate splits into two groups, and the split is about reference quality, not library quality:

  • Hosts with a genome of their own species map at 82–96 %.
  • The four Euonymus samples map at 31–36 %, because there is no E. japonicus assembly — the pipeline substitutes E. europaeus (GCA_963580455.1), a congener. Two thirds of those reads have nowhere to go.
In [6]:
def parse_hisat2(path):
    t = Path(path).read_text()
    g = lambda p: int(re.search(p, t).group(1))
    total = g(r"^(\d+) reads")
    return dict(
        total_pairs=total,
        conc_unique=g(r"(\d+) \([\d.]+%\) aligned concordantly exactly 1 time"),
        conc_multi=g(r"(\d+) \([\d.]+%\) aligned concordantly >1 times"),
        disc=g(r"(\d+) \([\d.]+%\) aligned discordantly 1 time"),
        overall=float(re.search(r"([\d.]+)% overall alignment rate", t).group(1)),
    )

aln = pd.DataFrame({s: parse_hisat2(ROOT / "02_align" / f"{s}.hisat2.log") for s in ORDER}).T
aln["conc_pct"] = 100 * (aln.conc_unique + aln.conc_multi) / aln.total_pairs

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.6))
barh(axes[0], aln.index, aln["overall"], hcolors, "{:.1f}%")
axes[0].set_title("Overall alignment rate"); axes[0].set_xlabel("% of reads aligned")
axes[0].set_xlim(0, 112); host_legend(axes[0])
note(axes[0], "Euonymus samples are aligned to E. europaeus, a congener proxy — the low rate is the\n"
              "missing reference, not the library.")

barh(axes[1], aln.index, aln["conc_pct"], [SERIES[0]] * len(aln), "{:.1f}%")
axes[1].set_title("Pairs aligning concordantly"); axes[1].set_xlabel("% of pairs")
axes[1].set_xlim(0, 112); axes[1].set_yticklabels([])
plt.tight_layout(); save(fig, "02_alignment"); plt.show()

4. The dual-RNA-seq split — and what the "bacterial" reads really are¶

This is the section that decides how the rest of the data can be used.

4a. The bacterial fraction is tiny¶

Between 0.004 % and 0.4 % of aligned reads land on the Agrobacterium genome. The two mutant samples (1416G-19CC547, 1416G-30CC547) are lower still, at 361 and 2,399 reads in a ~50 M-pair library.

4b. Those reads are almost all on one plasmid¶

Splitting the aligned bacterial reads by replicon shows they do not come from a bacterium transcribing its genome. In most samples 95–99 % sit on the Ti plasmid, which is 2 % of the genome, while the 2.8 Mb chromosome is nearly silent.

In [8]:
def idxstats(sample):
    df = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "02_align" / f"{sample}.idxstats", sep="\t",
                     names=["ref", "length", "mapped", "unmapped"])
    return df[df.ref.str.startswith("agro_")]

REPL = ["circ", "lin", "pAt1", "pAt2", "pTi"]
REPL_LABEL = {"circ": "circular chromosome", "lin": "linear chromosome",
              "pAt1": "pAt1", "pAt2": "pAt2", "pTi": "Ti plasmid"}
rep_reads, rep_len = {}, {}
for s in ORDER:
    d = idxstats(s)
    key = d.ref.str.rsplit("_", n=1).str[-1]
    rep_reads[s] = d.groupby(key).mapped.sum().reindex(REPL).fillna(0)
    rep_len[s] = d.groupby(key).length.first().reindex(REPL)
rep_reads = pd.DataFrame(rep_reads).T.loc[ORDER]
rep_len = pd.DataFrame(rep_len).T.loc[ORDER]
rep_share = 100 * rep_reads.div(rep_reads.sum(axis=1), axis=0)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, 4.8))
left = np.zeros(len(rep_share)); y = np.arange(len(rep_share))
for i, r in enumerate(REPL):
    ax.barh(y, rep_share[r], left=left, height=0.62, color=SERIES[i],
            edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1.2, label=REPL_LABEL[r])   # surface gap between segments
    left += rep_share[r].values
ax.set_yticks(y, rep_share.index); ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.set_xlim(0, 100); ax.set_xlabel("% of Agrobacterium reads")
ax.set_title("Where the Agrobacterium reads land")
clean(ax, "x"); ax.legend(loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.12), ncols=5)
for yi, v in zip(y, rep_share["pTi"]):
    ax.text(101, yi, f"pTi {v:.0f}%", va="center", fontsize=7.5, color=INK2)
plt.tight_layout(); save(fig, "04_replicon_share"); plt.show()

# Coverage density makes the size difference explicit: reads per kb of replicon.
dens = (rep_reads / (rep_len / 1000)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 4.4))
m = ax.imshow(np.log10(dens.values + 0.01), cmap=SEQ, aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(REPL)), [REPL_LABEL[r] for r in REPL], rotation=20, ha="right")
ax.set_yticks(range(len(dens)), dens.index)
ax.set_title("Read density per replicon — reads per kb")
ax.grid(False)
for i in range(dens.shape[0]):
    for j in range(dens.shape[1]):
        v = dens.values[i, j]
        ax.text(j, i, f"{v:,.1f}" if v >= 0.1 else ("0" if v == 0 else "<0.1"),
                ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7,
                color="white" if np.log10(v + 0.01) > 0.7 else INK)
fig.colorbar(m, ax=ax, shrink=0.8, label="colour scale: log₁₀ reads/kb")
plt.tight_layout(); save(fig, "05_replicon_density"); plt.show()

rep_share.round(2)

4c. And within the Ti plasmid, they sit inside the T-DNA¶

Plotting each Agrobacterium gene's counts against its position on the Ti plasmid puts essentially all of the signal in one contiguous 3–22 kb block. In strain 1416 that block is annotated, and it is unambiguous:

Gene Annotation Role
pTi.gene.5565 Tryptophan 2-monooxygenase iaaM — auxin synthesis
pTi.gene.5564 Indoleacetamide hydrolase iaaH — auxin synthesis
pTi.gene.5567 Isopentenyl transferase ipt — cytokinin synthesis
pTi.gene.5571 D-octopine dehydrogenase ocs — opine synthesis
pTi.gene.5563 Agrocinopine synthase acs — opine synthesis
pTi.gene.5562 RolB/RolC glucosidase family gene 5 / E

These are T-DNA genes — the segment Agrobacterium transfers into the plant nucleus. Once integrated they are transcribed by the plant's own polymerase, in plant cells, with plant promoters and polyadenylation. Those transcripts are in the host mRNA pool, and they align to the Ti plasmid because that is where the sequence came from.

So the "bacterial fraction" in section 4a is mostly plant transcription of integrated T-DNA, not the transcriptome of living bacteria. Three observations point the same way: the chromosome is silent while the T-DNA is not, the signal is confined to the T-DNA and stops at its borders, and the two mutants — the samples with essentially no T-DNA signal — are exactly the ones a disarmed or onc-mutant strain would produce.

Treat this as a strong reading of the coverage, not a settled fact: confirming it means checking strand and splicing at the T-DNA borders, and looking for plant-side polyadenylation.

In [9]:
def load_gff_genes(gff):
    rec = []
    for line in Path(gff).read_text().splitlines():
        if line.startswith("#") or "\tgene\t" not in line:
            continue
        f = line.split("\t")
        attr = dict(kv.split("=", 1) for kv in f[8].split(";") if "=" in kv)
        rec.append(dict(gene=attr.get("ID"), contig=f[0], start=int(f[3]), end=int(f[4]),
                        strand=f[6], name=attr.get("Name", "")))
    return pd.DataFrame(rec).set_index("gene")

STRAINS = {"1416": "strain_1416", "29": "strain_29"}
gff = {k: load_gff_genes(ROOT / "references" / "agrobacterium" / v / f"{v}.gff3")
       for k, v in STRAINS.items()}
mat = {k: pd.read_csv(ROOT / "04_matrix" / f"agro_{v}.tsv", sep="\t", index_col=0)
       for k, v in STRAINS.items()}

# Label only the handful of genes that carry the signal - never every point.
LABELS_1416 = {"agro_1416_pTi.gene.5562": "gene 5 / rolB-C",
               "agro_1416_pTi.gene.5563": "acs",
               "agro_1416_pTi.gene.5564": "iaaH",
               "agro_1416_pTi.gene.5565": "iaaM",
               "agro_1416_pTi.gene.5567": "ipt",
               "agro_1416_pTi.gene.5571": "ocs"}

# Two views per strain: the whole plasmid for context, and the T-DNA block on its
# own axis so the gene labels have room to sit without colliding.
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 8.6), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.4, 1]})
for row, strain in enumerate(["1416", "29"]):
    g, m = gff[strain], mat[strain]
    pti = g[g.contig == f"agro_{strain}_pTi"]
    tot = m.loc[m.index.intersection(pti.index)].sum(axis=1)
    d = pti.join(tot.rename("reads"), how="left").fillna({"reads": 0})
    hot = d.nlargest(8, "reads")
    lo, hi = hot.start.min() / 1000, hot.end.max() / 1000

    for col, ax in enumerate(axes[row]):
        x = d.start / 1000
        ax.vlines(x, 0, d.reads, color=GRID, linewidth=1)
        ax.scatter(x, d.reads, s=26, color=SERIES[0], zorder=3,
                   edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1)        # surface ring on overlapping marks
        ax.set_yscale("symlog", linthresh=10)
        ax.set_xlabel("position on pTi (kb)")
        clean(ax, "y")
        if col == 0:
            ax.axvspan(lo - 1, hi + 1, color=SERIES[3], alpha=0.13, zorder=0)
            ax.set_title(f"Strain {strain} — whole Ti plasmid")
            ax.set_ylabel("reads (all samples)")
            ax.annotate(f"T-DNA\n{lo:.0f}–{hi:.0f} kb", xy=((lo + hi) / 2, 0.94),
                        xycoords=("data", "axes fraction"), ha="center", va="top",
                        fontsize=8, color=INK2)
        else:
            ax.set_xlim(lo - 2.5, hi + 2.5)
            ax.set_title(f"Strain {strain} — T-DNA region, enlarged")
            if strain == "1416":
                # stagger the labels: these genes sit within a few hundred bp of each other
                for n, (gene, lab) in enumerate(sorted(
                        LABELS_1416.items(), key=lambda kv: d.start.get(kv[0], 0))):
                    if gene not in d.index:
                        continue
                    r = d.loc[gene]
                    ax.annotate(lab, (r.start / 1000, max(r.reads, 1)),
                                textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 11 + 13 * (n % 2)),
                                ha="center", fontsize=8.5, color=INK,
                                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=GRID, linewidth=0.8,
                                                shrinkA=0, shrinkB=3))
                ax.margins(y=0.30)
                ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
            else:
                note(ax, "RAST identifiers (fig|357.664.peg.N) carry no gene names, so this block is shown\n"
                         "by position only — the same contiguous, chromosome-silent pattern.", y=-0.22)

# Share of each sample's Agrobacterium reads that fall in the T-DNA window.
WINDOW = {"1416": (3_000, 22_000), "29": (78_000, 95_000)}

for strain, m in mat.items():
    g = gff[strain]
    pti = g[g.contig == f"agro_{strain}_pTi"]
    lo, hi = WINDOW[strain]

    for s in m.columns:

                         tdna=m.loc[m.index.intersection(tdna), s].sum(),
                         pct=100 * m.loc[m.index.intersection(tdna), s].sum() / tot if tot else np.nan))

5. Counting¶

featureCounts assignment, per sample. The pattern follows annotation availability, not data quality:

  • Annotated hosts (citrus, papaya, tomato) — 20–27 M pairs assigned.
  • Euonymus, mustard — near-zero assignment. Their assemblies have no gene models, so reads align and then have nothing to be counted into. This is why 04_matrix/ holds no plant matrix for them.
In [11]:
def fc_summary(sample):
    d = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "03_counts" / f"{sample}.txt.summary", sep="\t",
                    index_col=0).iloc[:, 0]
    return dict(assigned=d.get("Assigned", 0),
                no_features=d.get("Unassigned_NoFeatures", 0),
                multimapping=d.get("Unassigned_MultiMapping", 0),
                unmapped=d.get("Unassigned_Unmapped", 0),
                ambiguity=d.get("Unassigned_Ambiguity", 0))

fc = pd.DataFrame({s: fc_summary(s) for s in ORDER}).T.loc[ORDER]
fc_pct = 100 * fc.div(fc.sum(axis=1), axis=0)

CATS = [("assigned", "assigned to a gene"), ("no_features", "no gene model here"),
        ("multimapping", "multi-mapping"), ("unmapped", "unmapped"),
        ("ambiguity", "ambiguous")]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.8))
left = np.zeros(len(fc_pct)); y = np.arange(len(fc_pct))
for i, (c, lab) in enumerate(CATS):
    ax.barh(y, fc_pct[c], left=left, height=0.62, color=SERIES[i],
            edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1.2, label=lab)
    left += fc_pct[c].values
ax.set_yticks(y, fc_pct.index); ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.set_xlim(0, 100); ax.set_xlabel("% of read pairs")
ax.set_title("featureCounts assignment")
clean(ax, "x"); ax.legend(loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.12), ncols=5)
plt.tight_layout(); save(fig, "08_featurecounts"); plt.show()

6a. Plant expression¶

The citrus matrix is the only one with enough samples to look at structure: one native C. sinensis gall (29wtHC83) plus four Poncirus trifoliata galls mapped onto the sweet-orange annotation, since Poncirus has no gene models of its own.

In [14]:
def cpm_log(m, min_count=10):
    keep = m[(m.sum(axis=1) >= min_count)]
    return np.log2(1e6 * keep / keep.sum() + 1)

cit = plant.get("plant_citrus_sinensis")
lc = cpm_log(cit)
corr = lc.corr(method="spearman")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))
ax = axes[0]
m = ax.imshow(corr.values, cmap=SEQ, vmin=corr.values.min(), vmax=1)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(corr)), corr.columns, rotation=35, ha="right")
ax.set_yticks(range(len(corr)), corr.index)
ax.grid(False); ax.set_title("Citrus samples — Spearman correlation of log₂ CPM")
for i in range(len(corr)):
    for j in range(len(corr)):
        v = corr.values[i, j]
        ax.text(j, i, f"{v:.3f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7.5,
                color="white" if v > corr.values.min() + 0.6 * (1 - corr.values.min()) else INK)
fig.colorbar(m, ax=ax, shrink=0.75, label="Spearman ρ")

# PCA: few points, so direct-label every one and keep a single hue - no legend needed.
ax = axes[1]
X = lc.T.values
X = X - X.mean(0)
U, S, Vt = np.linalg.svd(X, full_matrices=False)
pcs = U * S
var = 100 * S**2 / (S**2).sum()
marker = {"1416": "o", "29": "s"}
for i, s in enumerate(lc.columns):
    ax.scatter(pcs[i, 0], pcs[i, 1], s=90, color=SERIES[0],
               marker=marker[str(meta.loc[s, "strain"])], edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1.5, zorder=3)
    ax.annotate(s, (pcs[i, 0], pcs[i, 1]), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 12),
                ha="center", fontsize=8, color=INK)
ax.set_xlabel(f"PC1 ({var[0]:.0f}% of variance)"); ax.set_ylabel(f"PC2 ({var[1]:.0f}%)")
ax.set_title("Citrus samples — PCA of log₂ CPM")
ax.margins(0.22); clean(ax, "both")
ax.legend(handles=[mpl.lines.Line2D([], [], marker=marker[k], linestyle="", color=SERIES[0],
                                    markeredgecolor=SURFACE, label=f"strain {k}") for k in marker],
          loc="best")
note(ax, "n = 5 with no biological replication: this shows how the libraries sit relative to each\n"
         "other, and cannot separate strain, host or age effects.")
plt.tight_layout(); save(fig, "10_citrus_structure"); plt.show()

6b. Bacterial expression¶

For completeness: what is actually in the Agrobacterium matrices. Each sample's counts are dominated by a handful of T-DNA genes, and the totals are five orders of magnitude below the plant matrices.

7. Where this leaves the experiment¶

Usable now

  • Host transcriptomes for citrus (5), tomato (2) and papaya (1) — 20–27 M assigned pairs each, 65–91 % of gene models detected. Solid libraries.
  • T-DNA expression in the gall, per sample, as a quantitative readout of how strongly the integrated oncogenes are transcribed.

Not usable as it stands

  • Agrobacterium transcriptomes. At 0.004–0.4 % bacterial reads, and with that fraction dominated by plant-transcribed T-DNA, there is no chromosomal signal to analyse — 6–300 genes detected of ~5,800. More depth will not fix this. The read composition (rRNA 0.3–3 %, small non-coding RNAs absent, 95–98 % protein-coding) says these are polyA-selected libraries, and bacterial mRNA is not polyadenylated — it is excluded by the preparation, not merely under-sampled. See section 6 of 02_dataset_structure.ipynb. Recovering the bacterial transcriptome needs rRNA depletion without polyA capture.
  • Euonymus and mustard host expression, until an annotated genome is available. Reads exist; gene models do not.
  • Anything requiring replication. One library per gall, so between-group differences here cannot be separated from between-sample variation.

Worth checking next

  • Confirm the T-DNA reading — strand and splicing at the borders, plant-side polyadenylation — and confirm the library preparation against the sequencing provider's record, since the protocol written down in the repo describes the 2019 reference paper rather than these galls.
  • 1416G-19CC547 and 1416G-30CC547 show essentially no T-DNA signal. If those mutants are disarmed or onc-region mutants that is the expected result and a useful internal control; worth confirming against the strain records.
  • A Liftoff annotation from C. sinensis onto P. trifoliata would let the four CC samples be counted on their own genome instead of a cross-species proxy.
